scope.working_title: Data-efficient, on-device detection of Sinhala synthetic speech under call-channel distortion
scope.target: Synthetic/voice-converted versus bona fide speech; not speaker identity, truth of statements, scam intent or proof of fraud.
scope.prototype: Replay existing licensed recordings in causal chunks on an ordinary phone, or use app-owned audio. Do not assume access to native cellular calls or other apps' VoIP audio.
scope.constraints: One shared problem; three independently assessable research contributions; 6–8 months; existing data; no paid APIs or guaranteed high-end GPU; no participant recruitment.

proposed_investigations.question: At a fixed small Sinhala label budget, can source-balanced adaptation improve unseen-generator detection relative to ordinary fine-tuning?
proposed_investigations.hypothesis: Controlling source/language shortcuts improves transfer to held-out synthesis families.
proposed_investigations.rival: Gains reflect recording provenance or known generator artifacts.
proposed_investigations.method: Compact or parameter-efficient target adaptation against a frozen/shared teacher.
proposed_investigations.ablation: Remove source balancing at matched label/model/compute budget.
proposed_investigations.independent_result: Generator-held-out detection at several declared Sinhala data budgets.

proposed_investigations.question: Can channel-aware distillation/compression preserve detection after codec distortion better than standard compact or INT8 controls?
proposed_investigations.hypothesis: Training the compact model on matched real/fake channel views preserves useful evidence.
proposed_investigations.rival: Plain augmentation or a larger student explains the benefit.
proposed_investigations.method: Train a compact student with matched-domain distillation or quantisation-aware adaptation.
proposed_investigations.ablation: Teacher objective, channel views and quantisation separately.
proposed_investigations.independent_result: Error–memory–latency trade-off measured on a named ordinary phone.

proposed_investigations.question: Can causal score accumulation reduce early false alarms without excessive delay under changing channel quality?
proposed_investigations.hypothesis: An evidence-aware stopping policy improves the delay/error/coverage trade-off.
proposed_investigations.rival: A tuned fixed prefix or sequential threshold is equally effective.
proposed_investigations.method: Train/calibrate a bounded-state prefix decision model; compare existing sequential policies.
proposed_investigations.ablation: History, quality conditioning and stopping rule separately.
proposed_investigations.independent_result: Prefix error and decision delay; continuous-call false alarms only with suitable existing long recordings.

baselines: MFCC/LFCC + random forest or logistic model
Strong pretrained SSL + detection head as teacher/control
Ordinary fine-tuning, standard distillation, FP32/INT8 and fixed-prefix/sequential-threshold controls
evaluation.splits: Speaker-, source-utterance- and generator-family-aware groups; all derived channel versions stay together. Hold out real sources and channels where feasible; lock thresholds on development data.
evaluation.metrics: EER/ROC or PR metrics plus false-positive operating points, prefix accuracy, abstention/coverage and decision delay. Report device p50/p95 inference, memory, model size, hop throughput and sustained performance.
evaluation.latency: Audio accumulation + feature look-ahead + processing + decision confirmation. RTF below one is not proof of a short time-to-alert; overlapping-window compute must fit the hop interval.
evaluation.negative_findings: Show that language shift vanishes after source controls, that standard INT8 suffices, or that a given short prefix cannot support reliable decisions.
evaluation.claim_limits: Read-speech and synthetic-channel experiments do not establish safety or detection reliability in actual Sinhala calls. Synthetic detection does not prove malicious intent.

verdict: Conditional neighbourhood worth investigating; not qualified and no numeric topic score assigned. Generic Sinhala classification, short-input detection, codec robustness and quantisation are already studied. Sinhala multi-generator labelled data and a narrow methodological distinction remain unresolved.
next_decision: Secure an existing licensed Sinhala bona fide/spoof corpus or a permitted multi-generator derivative route before selecting the topic; then compare a strong baseline on held-out generators and call-like prefixes.
limitations: This is a bounded exploratory search, not a systematic review or novelty certification.
Eight scholarly discovery queries returned 125 result occurrences; many were irrelevant. Duplication outputs are retrieval leads, not proof of originality.
Direct full methods for the Sinhala 2025 paper and the ternary paper were unavailable; absence of a method detail in an abstract is not evidence it was not studied.
No call audio captured, accounts accessed, licence terms accepted, speech generated, weights loaded, audio downloaded or model/device performance measured.
Some newly discovered resources may have evolving dates or releases; no post-2026-10-29 paper is used as supporting evidence.
Raw abstract text is omitted from the archived index records; identifiers, links and access limits preserve the retrieval route.
